tells.2: Stacked slogans and balanced fragments—“A little measuring done. A little joy delivered.”—make it feel assembled from lifestyle-copy formulas.
tells.3: The familiar trio of stirring, baking, and sneaking a taste, followed by generic encouragement, feels templated.
tells.4: The tea-and-last-crumb imagery feels borrowed from a familiar cozy-brand vocabulary, though the phrasing is otherwise natural.

reason: Version 1 offers concrete reasons to trust and choose the product: a named supplier, a customer story, and evidence of popularity, assuming those claims are verified. Its crowded middle section needs tightening, but it has more substance and individuality than the others; these stylistic judgments do not establish authorship.
